fact: Oia's white villages sit on the rim of a drowned volcanic caldera, formed by one of the largest eruptions in recorded history.
name: Santorini, Greece

fact: This 15th-century Inca citadel sits 2,430m up in the Andes — and was never found by the Spanish conquistadors.
name: Machu Picchu, Peru

fact: Completed in 1889, the 330m tower was the world's tallest structure for 41 years — and grows ~15cm taller in summer heat.
name: Eiffel Tower, Paris

fact: The aurora borealis appears when charged solar particles collide with Earth's atmosphere near the poles.
name: Kirkjufell, Iceland

fact: Stretching over 21,000km, its many sections were built across 2,000 years — mostly during the Ming dynasty.
name: Great Wall, China

fact: Thousands of vermilion torii gates wind 4km up the mountain — each donated by a business praying for success.
name: Fushimi Inari, Kyoto

fact: The pyramid-shaped peak (4,478m) straddles Switzerland and Italy, reflected here under the Milky Way.
name: Matterhorn, Switzerland

fact: Al-Khazneh, 'The Treasury', was carved directly into rose-red sandstone cliffs over 2,000 years ago.
name: Petra, Jordan

fact: The lagoon's unreal turquoise comes from white coral sand reflecting sunlight through shallow, clear water.
name: Bora Bora, French Polynesia

fact: Flash floods sculpted these smooth sandstone waves over millions of years; light beams appear around midday in summer.
name: Antelope Canyon, USA
